title: Three strips of mesoderm

objective.text: Describe how mesoderm beside the midline divides into three strips and what each strip builds.

body.general: What happens to the middle layer beside the embryo's midline? By about day 17, this mesoderm (the middle germ layer) thickens into paraxial mesoderm [f1]. Further out it stays thin, as the lateral plate [f2]. A narrow strip, intermediate mesoderm, links the two [f3]. Paraxial mesoderm will break into paired blocks called somites [f4]. Intermediate mesoderm will build the kidneys and sex glands, or gonads [f5]. The lateral plate splits into two layers [f6]. The outer one builds the limb skeleton [f7]; the inner one wraps the gut [f8].
body.mbbs: By about day 17, intraembryonic mesoderm next to the midline thickens into paraxial mesoderm [f1]. More laterally it stays thin as the lateral plate mesoderm [f2]. Intermediate mesoderm is the narrow strip joining the two [f3]. Paraxial mesoderm goes on to form somites, paired blocks flanking the neural tube [f4]. Intermediate mesoderm gives the urogenital system, including the excretory units of the kidney and the gonads [f5]. Cavities in the lateral plate merge and split it into two layers [f6]. The parietal (somatic) layer forms limb bones and connective tissue, the dermis of the limbs and body wall, and the sternum [f7]. The visceral (splanchnic) layer joins the endoderm to form the gut wall [f8].

facts.text: By about day 17, mesoderm right beside the midline thickens into paraxial mesoderm.
Further from the midline, the mesoderm stays thin as the lateral plate.
Intermediate mesoderm is the narrow strip that links paraxial mesoderm and the lateral plate.
Paraxial mesoderm goes on to form somites, paired blocks beside the neural tube.
Intermediate mesoderm forms the urogenital system: the kidney's excretory units and the gonads.
Small cavities in the lateral plate merge and split it into two layers.
The parietal (outer) layer of the lateral plate forms limb bones and connective tissue, limb and body-wall dermis, and the sternum.
The visceral (inner) layer of the lateral plate, with the endoderm, forms the gut wall.

misconceptions.right: Limb bones and connective tissue come from lateral plate mesoderm; only limb muscles come from somites.

misconceptions.wrong: Somites are segments of the neural tube.
misconceptions.right: Somites are blocks of paraxial mesoderm lying beside the neural tube (future spinal cord).

checks.prompt: Put the three mesoderm strips in order, from the midline outward.
checks.why: Paraxial mesoderm is thick and next to the midline; the lateral plate is thin and furthest out; intermediate mesoderm links them.

checks.prompt: Which strip builds the kidneys and the sex glands?
checks.why: Intermediate mesoderm forms the urinary and genital organs.

checks.prompt: Limb bones and their connective tissue come from which source?
options: The outer layer of the lateral plate
checks.why: The outer layer of the lateral plate makes limb bones and connective tissue; somites add only the limb muscles.

adult: These strips become the kidneys and gonads [f5], the limb skeleton and sternum [f7], and the gut wall [f8].

remember.q: Which three mesoderm strips lie beside the midline, from inside out?
remember.a: Paraxial mesoderm, intermediate mesoderm, then the lateral plate [f1,f2,f3].
The kidneys and the sex glands (gonads) [f5].

remember.q: What splits the lateral plate into two layers?
remember.a: Small cavities inside it that merge [f6].
